title: Signed cochain assembly of a natural additive dual comparison
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $(\mathcal C,J)$ a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use $B$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and internal Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $T:R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ be an additive functor (it preserves addition of morphisms). For every $R$-module $V$ suppose a $B$-linear sheaf morphism $\eta_V:T(V^*)\to\mathcal Hom_B(TV,B)$ is given, where $V^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$, with
$$\mathcal Hom_B(Tf,1_B)\circ\eta_W=\eta_V\circ T(f^*)\quad(f:V\to W).$$
Let $F^\bullet$ be any integer cochain complex of $R$-modules and put $F^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(F,R[0])$ using the module-valued total Hom complex [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Its coordinate in degree $q$ is $(F^{-q})^*$, with differential $\phi\mapsto-(-1)^q\phi d_F^{-q-1}$. Apply $T$ termwise to complexes and write $D(TF,B)$ for the signed sheaf dual of [def-sc-signed-sheaf-dual-complex]. The morphisms $\eta_{F^{-q}}$, preceded by $T$ of the scalar coordinate isomorphisms, define a unique chain map
$$\kappa_F:T(F^\vee)\longrightarrow D(TF,B).$$
Its differential compatibility in these coordinates is
$$d_D^q\eta_{F^{-q}}=\eta_{F^{-q-1}}T\bigl(-(-1)^q(d_F^{-q-1})^*\bigr).$$
It is contravariantly natural in cochain maps $F\to G$. If all $\eta_{F^r}$ are isomorphisms, $\kappa_F$ is an isomorphism of cochain complexes, and its localization is an isomorphism in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $F^r=0$ outside $[a,b]$, both $T(F^\vee)$ and $D(TF,B)$ vanish outside $[-b,-a]$, including for the zero complex and $a>b$. No exactness of $T$ or finite projectivity of $F^r$ is required.

proof.text: Write $\tau_q:(F^\vee)^q\xrightarrow{\sim}(F^{-q})^*$ for projection to the factor $p=-q$ in [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Every other factor has target $R[0]^{p+q}=0$. The inverse inserts a functional into that factor and zero into all other factors; both composites are identities and both maps are $R$-linear. The target differential is zero, so the defining total-Hom differential gives $\tau_{q+1}d_{F^\vee}^q=\epsilon_q(d_F^{-q-1})^*\tau_q$, where $\epsilon_q=-(-1)^q\in\{1,-1\}$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, specialized to target R[0]; scalar analogue in more-algebra.tex, Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes.

proof.text: Additivity gives $T(0)=0$ by cancelling in $T(0)=T(0)+T(0)$, and $T(-g)=-T(g)$ by applying $T$ to $g+(-g)=0$. Thus $T(\epsilon_qg)=\epsilon_qT(g)$. Applying $T$ degreewise is legitimate: $T(d^{q+1})T(d^q)=T(d^{q+1}d^q)=0$, and functoriality sends the chain-map equations to chain-map equations. Morphisms and their identities are the degreewise ones of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; addition and cancellation for module-sheaf maps are sectionwise in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 0A8X, signed Hom differential; elementary additive-functor identities, agent-written.

proof.text: For a module map $g$, put $H(g)=\mathcal Hom_B(Tg,1_B)$; on every localized site it sends $h$ to $h\circ Tg$ by [def-pur-sheaf-hom], so it is additive in $g$. For $d=d_F^{-q-1}$ the supplied naturality gives $H(d)\eta_{F^{-q}}=\eta_{F^{-q-1}}T(d^*)$. Multiplication by $\epsilon_q$ and Step 2 give $d_D^q\eta_{F^{-q}}=\epsilon_qH(d)\eta_{F^{-q}}=\eta_{F^{-q-1}}T(\epsilon_qd^*)$, using exactly the differential of [def-sc-signed-sheaf-dual-complex]. Set $\kappa_F^q=\eta_{F^{-q}}T(\tau_q)$. Step 1 now yields $d_D^q\kappa_F^q=\kappa_F^{q+1}T(d_{F^\vee}^q)$. This is the chain-map equation; a chain map with these components is unique since equality of chain maps is degreewise.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, sign convention; agent-written assembly from the assumed naturality equation.

proof.text: For a cochain map $f:F\to G$, scalar precomposition has degree-$q$ coordinate $(f^{-q})^*$. It commutes with the signed differentials because $f^{-q}d_F^{-q-1}=d_G^{-q-1}f^{-q-1}$: applying a functional $\phi$ gives $\epsilon_q\phi f^{-q}d_F^{-q-1}=\epsilon_q\phi d_G^{-q-1}f^{-q-1}$. Sheaf precomposition $H(f^{-q})$ is a cochain map for the same displayed equation after applying $T$. Naturality of $\eta$ and the coordinate projection give $H(f^{-q})\kappa_G^q=\eta_{F^{-q}}T((f^{-q})^*)T(\tau_q^G)=\kappa_F^qT((f^\vee)^q)$. These are all components of the required contravariant naturality square. Precomposition reverses composites and preserves identities, so these squares are natural for the contravariant dual functors.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes; direct precomposition calculation, agent-written.

proof.text: If the specified $\eta_{F^r}$ are invertible, set $\lambda^q=T(\tau_q^{-1})\eta_{F^{-q}}^{-1}$. Functoriality gives $\lambda^q\kappa_F^q=1$ and $\kappa_F^q\lambda^q=1$. Multiplying the chain-map equation of Step 3 on its two sides by these inverses gives $T(d_{F^\vee}^q)\lambda^q=\lambda^{q+1}d_D^q$. Hence $\lambda$ is an inverse chain map. For the localization functor $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q(\lambda)Q(\kappa_F)=Q(1)=1$ and $Q(\kappa_F)Q(\lambda)=1$, which proves the derived isomorphism without constructing a derived functor of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, ordinary complexes; elementary inverse and functoriality calculation, agent-written.

proof.text: The identity of $T(0)$ equals $T(1_0)=T(0)=0$. Evaluating on every object of the site shows every section of $T(0)$ is zero. Thus $T$ takes zero modules to zero sheaves, and also takes any module isomorphic to zero to a zero sheaf. If $q<-b$ or $q>-a$, then $-q>b$ or $-q<a$, so $F^{-q}=0$ and $(F^{-q})^*=0$. Step 1 and the preceding observation give $T(F^\vee)^q=0$. Also $(TF)^{-q}=0$, and [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives $D(TF,B)^q=\mathcal Hom_B(0,B)=0$, since every localized module map from zero is zero. The same reasoning applies for every $q$ when $a>b$, and for the zero complex; no endpoint or nonzero assumption was used.
